items.title: Charlie Hamilton Interview, 1965-03-21
items.q: I think I heard you the first time, it was across the river, along the west we go, along that road that goes up the river, with Ezreal Gorman one night, and Jim Robinson.

ctx.x: Talbert. In Howard, they were the two trumpet players, George Lewis, Lawrence Marrero, Jim Robinson.

I think I heard you the first time, it was across the river, along the west we go, along that road that goes up the river, with Ezreal Gorman one night, and Jim Robinson. I don't know, it wasn't anybody's special, organized band, it just happened to be a pickup band, but that's the first time I ever saw you and got to hear you. Then I didn't hear you for a few years, until you were here on Bourbon Street with George and all that. Yeah. I believe.
No, since I'm out freeing them, getting around, around there, and going there, I mean I have a chance. I think I'll make the trip with George, he want me to go to Japan.

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-07-13
items.q: Charlie Hamilton was playing piano, yeah.

ctx.x: And he had, and he had, uh, Tag of Flowers too. Yeah. He used to be staying.
Charlie Hamilton was playing with you, remember? Charlie Hamilton was playing piano, yeah.
And the Cuckoo was playing trumpet. Playing trumpet, yeah. And we worked there a year and, but six months.
